children.prompt: kite, $PQRS$, with $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PSR$ both obtuse

answer.short: One possible sketch is shown, with $PQ=PS$, $QR=SR$ and both $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PSR$ obtuse.
answer.worked: Place $Q$ and $S$ symmetrically above and below $PR$, closer to $R$ than to $P$. Join $P,Q,R,S$ in order. This gives $PQ=PS$ and $QR=SR$; choose the height so that both $\angle PQR$ and $\angle PSR$ exceed $90^{\circ}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6c, supplied sketch in the right cell
spec.description: P is left, R right, Q above and S below. Q and S are vertically aligned and nearer R. P and R are horizontally aligned. Point markers and labels are retained; no equality ticks, diagonals or angle arcs are added.
spec.mathematics: Reflection in PR gives PQ=PS and QR=SR. The vectors from Q towards P and R have a negative dot product, so angle PQR is obtuse; reflection gives the same obtuse angle at S. Coordinates reconstruct an illustrative valid sketch without introducing numerical givens.
